root_cause.text: In the bnxt_re RDMA hardware counter enum, three generic counters were incorrectly added after the BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR boundary marker used to size hw_stats allocations, causing bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() to write stats entries past the BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS-allocated array.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR acts as a boundary marker for allocating hardware statistics with different num_counters,” that placing the new counters after it caused “BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS [to be] used when allocating hw_stats,” and the patch fixes this by moving BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR in hw_counters.h.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add new hardware statistic identifiers for CQE and remote access error reporting in bnxt_re.
intent_record.what: Three new enum constants were added to the bnxt_re_hw_stats enumeration: BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS.
intent_record.how: This extends the set of hardware statistics identifiers so the driver can represent and potentially collect/report request CQE errors, response CQE errors, and response remote access errors at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove three invalid or unsupported hardware statistic entries from bnxt_re_hw_stats so the exported extended counter set matches actual runtime-supported stats.
intent_record.what: Three enum constants were removed from the bnxt_re_hw_stats enumeration: BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS, while BNXT_RE_NUM_EXT_COUNTERS remains as the terminating count entry.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these three hardware statistic identifiers are no longer part of the extended counters set, reducing the number of indexed stats and preventing code from exposing or referencing these specific counters through this enum-based stats table.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability was caused by adding new generic hardware counters in the bnxt_re enum beyond the boundary marker used for allocation sizing. This group adds new hardware statistic identifiers in that area, directly matching the root cause of the out-of-bounds stats write.

The vulnerability is caused by three extra generic counters being included beyond the boundary used to size hardware stats arrays, leading to out-of-bounds writes. This change removes those three invalid/unsupported stat entries from bnxt_re_hw_stats, directly addressing the mismatched counter set that caused the overflow.

candidates.rationale: This generic counter was incorrectly included in the enum after the standard-counter boundary, contributing to a mismatch between the allocated BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS-sized array and the indices written by bnxt_re_copy_err_stats().
This counter extended the enum beyond the BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR standard-counter boundary, making later writes index past the hw_stats allocation sized by BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS.
This misplaced generic counter was one of the extra entries beyond the standard counter boundary and directly enabled out-of-bounds stats writes when error stats were copied.
This boundary marker defines the end of standard counters used for sizing hw_stats allocations; placing generic counters after it caused the array-size/index mismatch underlying the overflow.

vuln_statements.explanation: This enum entry was incorrectly added after the BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR boundary that determines BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS sizing, so later stats-copy code could use this index against an array allocated only for standard counters, causing out-of-bounds writes.

This counter extended the enum beyond the standard-counter boundary marker while hw_stats allocation still used BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS, contributing directly to the index/allocation mismatch that enabled out-of-bounds writes.
This misplaced enum entry was one of the extra generic counters after the sizing boundary, so writes to this stat index could go past the BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS-allocated hw_stats array.

That matches the root cause exactly: generic counters were incorrectly added after the boundary marker used to size hw_stats allocations, enabling writes past the standard-counter array.
